RULES MADE IN TERMS OF BY-LAW 23 OF THE REGISTERED BY-LAWS OF MULTI-PURPOSE
CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETY LIMITEDS OF THE NORTH WESTERN PROVINCE

BY virtue of the powers vested in me by By-law 23 of the registered By-laws of a Multi-Purpose Co-operative Society, I,Dissanayake Mudiyanselage Kulamina Chandana Dissanayake, Commissioner of Co-operative Development and Registrarof Co-operative Societies, of the North Western Province, do by this Order hereby make the following Rules for the electionof a Branch Committee .of a Co-operative Society.
D .M.K.C. DISSANAYAKE,Commissioner of Co-operative Development
and Registrar of Co-operative Societies.
Kurunegala,25th February 2015.
1. Short Title :
These Rules may be cited as Rules for the election of a Branch Committee of Multi-Purpose Co-operative Societiesin the North Western Province.
2. Voters' List :
2.1 For the purpose of electing the required number of Branch Committee members

under By-law 22(1) of a Multi-Purpose Co-operative Society, a list of members who are eligible to vote shall beprepared in triplicate for each year ending 31st December of every year by the Board of Directors. Such list shall be preparedprior to 15th January of the ensuing year.

One of these lists shall be exhibited in a prominent place in the office of the Branch and another copy of it in aprominent place of business in the Branch for a period from 16th January to 31st January each year.

However, a list of members of any Co-operative Society for the year ending on the last day of a month whichpresides three months of the date fixed for the election of the Society shall be prepared prior to the 15th day of the ensuing

month and such list shall be so exhibited from the 16th day to the last day of the ensuing month and amendments, if any,pertaining to appeals submitted shall be made in the list on or before 15th day of the ensuing month.

2.2 Any person who is qualified to have his or her name entered in the list referred to in Rule 2.1 above and whosename has not been included in such list, may appeal to the Secretary to the Society within the period from the 16th day to thelast day of the month during which the list is exhibited to have his or her name included in such list. Such appeal shall bedisposed of by the Board of Directors and amendments, if any, shall be made in the list on or before 15th day of the ensuingmonth.

2.3 Any member of the Society whose name is registered in that Branch may object in writing to the secretary of thatSociety and state the reasons therefor, to the appearance of a name in the list referred to in Rule 2.1 within the period from the16th day of the month the list has been exhibited· until the last day of the month. Such objections shall be disposed of by theBoard of Directors and amendments, if any, shall be made in the list on or before 15th day of the ensuing month.

2.4 If the appeals referred to in Rule 2.2 and the objections referred to in Rule 2.3 are not disposed of by the Boardof Directors within the stipulated, time, the Commissioner of Co-operative Development and the Registrar of Co-operativeSocieties may direct such Board of Directors to dispose of the objections and cause the list of members eligible to vote to berevised, if necessary. The Society should comply therewith accordingly. The Secretary of the Society shall revise the Voters’list and the President and another Director of the Society shall certify same.

2.5 At every instance where an election is held, the Board of Directors of the Society shall furnish to the Commissionerof Co-operative Development and the Registrar of Co-operative Societies a certified copy of the final Voters’ list of eachbranch within 7 days of such certification and two copies certified by the Commissioner of Co-operative Development andthe Registrar of Co-operative Societies shall be returned to the society and elections shall thereafter be held on such Voters’list.

2.6 If the list referred to in Rule 2. 1 is not prepared by the Society or is not revised by the Board of Directors in termsRule 2.2 and 2.3 and duly certified in terms of Rule 2 .4 and made available to the Commissioner of Co-operative Developmentand the Registrar of Co-operative Societies under Rule 2.5, the Commissioner of Co-operative Development and the Registrarof Co-operative Societies shall cause such list of members who are eligible to vote to be prepared by some other officer,certify such list and it shall be lawful to hold elections on such Voters’ list. It shall also be lawful to recover the expensesincurred thereon from the defaulting Board of Directors of the Society.
General
APPOINTMENT OF CHIEF ELECTIONS OFFICER, ELECTIONS OFFICERS IN-CHARGE OF ZONES AND ASSISTANT
ELECTIONS OFFICERS

3.1 The Commissioner shall appoint for every Multi-Purpose Co-operative Society a Chief Elections Officer, ElectionsOfficers In-Charge of Zones and Assistant Elections Officers as may be necessary under these Rules. Such appointmentshall be in the form Specified in Schedule “A”.
3.2 The Elections Officers so appointed by the Commissioner shall exercise all such powers referred to in theseRules except those reserved for the Commissioner.

3.3 The Secretary of the Society shall furnish to the Commissioner the particulars of the Branches where theelections are to be held three months prior to the expiry of their terms and the Commissioner may fix in advance the datesbefore which nominations shall be called and the elections shall be held. The Commissioner shall have the power to very suchorder.

3.4 The Chief Elections Officer, Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones and Assistant Elections Officers shall beresponsible for the proper conduct of the elections from the time nominations are called and up to the time the results areannounced and communicated to the society in terms of Rule 8.1 and 13.2 of those Rules and shall work under the directionof the Commissioner.

3.5 The Elections Officer shall give the Secretary of the Society at least 7 days notice in writing of the Date, time andplace where the nomination papers and the objections to such nominations will be received by him.

3. 6 The Elections Officer shall at the same time send to each Branch sufficient number of copies of such notice tobe exhibited at the Head Office of the Society and at the branch and other prominent places within the area of operations ofthe branch.

3.7 Elections to Branch Committees shall take place at such place, or places as may be determined by the ChiefElections Officer, Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones and Assistant Elections Officers on the latest certified copy of thevoters list referred to in Rule 2.5 or 2.6.

3.8 The Board of Directors of the Society and the Staff employed by such society shall render such assistance usmay be required by the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones/Assistant Elections Officers underthese Rules.
Part II
DISQUALIFICATIONS
4.1 No member shall be nominated for election or be elected to a Branch Committee of a Society if he : -
(a) is a person whose name does not appear in the Voters' List of the Branch ;
(b) is below the age of 18 years ;
(c) has within 3 immediately proceeding years been convicted of a criminal offence or has been sentenced to a
term of imprisonment exceeding three months or such sentence has been suspended ;
(d) has filed a declaration of insolvency or is adjudicated an insolvent ;
(e) is in default for three months or above in respect of any loan or any surcharge payable under Section 44(6)
of the Co-operative Law or any other dues payable in terms of any regulation made under Section 66 to thissociety or to any either registered co-operative society;
(f) is registered as a trader with this Society or is carrying on business which conflicts with the interests of the
society;
(g) holds any office or place of profit under the society or receives any honorarium without the prior approval
of the Commissioner;
(h) is a paid employee of the Society or any other registered society ;
(i) is directly or indirectly interested, save in his capacity as a member, in any contract made with the society or
in any sale or purchase made by the society, or in any contract or transaction of the society which concernsthe finances of the society and which is either subsisting or in the course of negotiation;
(j) is a person who, within the last 5 years has had, to vacate his office or employment in terms of Rules made
under the Co-operative Law;

branch for a period less than one year immediately presiding the date of receiving nominations, providedhowever, this provision shall not be applicable to any person who has not been a member of the immediateExecutive Committee or the Board of Directors of the Society ;
(m) is a person who ceased to be a member to the date specified for receipt of nomination papers;
(n) is a person in respect of whom a period 3 years has not elapsed since he has paid the amount in full specified
in the awarded of arbitration under Section 58 of the Co-operative Act, in the surcharge imposed undersection 44(6) or in the ordered under section 66.
NOMINATIONS

5.1 Nomination Paper Every candidate who stands for election to the Branch Committee shall be proposed by amember of the Society and shall be seconded by another member of the Society. Each candidate, his proposer and secondershall be members of the Society whose names appear in the Voters’ List of the Branch to which elections are to be held. Thenomination of each candidate shall be in writing on the form specified in Schedule “B” of these Rules.
DECLARATION BY A CANDIDATE, PROPOSER AND SECONDER
5.2 Each candidate shall attach to his nomination paper a declaration in the form specified in Schedule “c” of theseRules.
5.3 Each such Proposer and Seconder shall likewise make a declaration in the form specified in Schedule “C 1 ” ofthese Rules.
RECEIVING NOMINATION PAPERS

6.1 On the day fixed for notifications for elections to a Branch Committee of a Society the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer; In-Charge of Zones/Assistant Elections Officer shall be present at the place fixed for receipt of suchnominations and shall receive such nomination papers as may be handed in.

6.2 Each nomination paper shall he prepared in quadruplicate in the form set out in Schedule “B” and signed by theProposer and Seconder and the candidate and handed in by the candidate himself or his Proposer or Seconder together withthe declarations made under Schedule “C” and “Cl” between the hours 9.00 am. and 10.00 pm on the day fixed for suchnomination to . the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones/Assistant Elections Officers.

6.3 On receipt of such nomination paper, the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of Zones/AssistantElections Officer shall verify that the candidate, the Proposer and Seconder are not disqualified under Rule 4. 1 of these Rulesand shall reject the nomination of the candidate who is so disqualified or whose nomination is not in conformity with Rule 5.1or 5.2 or 5.3 of these Rules.

6.4 The Elections Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones/Assistant Elections Officers shallthereafter cause two copies of each Nomination Paper as is not rejected by him under Rule 6. 3 above, to be conspicuouslydisplayed at the place where those nominations are received.
RECEIVING OF OBJECTIONS

7.1 Any person whose name appears in the Voters’ list of the Branch in which elections are to be held may fileobjections to any nomination. Such objections shall be in writing and shall be handed into the Chief Elections Officer/

Elections Officer In-Charge of the Zone/Assistant Elections Officer between 10.00 a.m. and 11.00 am. on the day suchnomination papers are accepted by the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of the Zone/Assistant ElectionsOfficer
7.2 The objections to any nomination shall be only on grounds specified below:
(a) the candidate or the proposer or the seconder of the candidate is disqualified under one or more provisions
or rule 4.1 above;
(b) the candidate or the proposer or the seconder of the candidate is not a person whose name appears in the
voters’ list;
(c) the candidate or the proposer or the seconder of the candidate has not submitted the nomination.

7.3 Where the Chief Elections Officerl/Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones/Assistant Elections Officers upholdsan objection under Rule 7(b) and (c) above, he shall reject the nomination paper in regard to which the objection was made

7.4 Notwithstanding any objection under Rule 7.2(a) above, the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officers In-Chargeof Zones/Assistant Elections Officers shall proceed with the , election on the basis of nominations accepted by him. All suchobjections under Rule 7.2(a) shall be forwarded to the Commissioner and his decision thereon is final and conclusive.

7.5 Any objection under rule 7.2(e) is upheld by the Commissioner, the election of such candidate shall, ipso facto,be null and void. The vacancy occurring in the Committee as a result of this decision shall be filled in accordance with the By-Laws of the Society.
JOURNAL

7.6 Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones/Assistant Elections Officers shall maintain ajournal which shall be in two parts. One copy shall be forwarded to the Society concerned and the other copy to the AssistantCommissioner of Co-operative Development of the area. The objections received in writing under 7 .2(a) shall be forwardedto the Assistant Commissioner of Co-operative Development by the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officers In-Charge ofZones/Assistant Elections Officers. The objections received in writing under 7 .2(b) shall be forwarded by the Chief ElectionsOfficer/Elections Officers In-Charge of Zones/Assistant Elections Officers to the Assistant Commissioner of Co-operativeDevelopment of the area,
Following items shall be recorded in Part I.
(a) Name and address of the Society
(b) Number and address of the Branch
(c) Names of candidates whose nominations papers were received and the time of receipts
(d) Names and addresses of persons who handed in objections under Rules 7.1 of these rules and the time of
receipt of such objections.
(e) Names of candidates whose nominations were rejected by him and the reasons for such rejection.
(f) Names of candidates against whom objections were received under 7.2(e) and 7.2(b) separately
(g) The symbols allotted to the candidate and the serial number allotted under Rule 9.2

Part III
ELECTIONS PROCEDURE
8.1 Uncontested Elections

Where the number of candidates duly nominated to nine or less and more than 5, each candidate shall be deemed tobe elected and the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of the zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall issue astatement in writing to the Secretary of the Society to that effect.
8.2 Contested Elections

Where the number of candidates duly nominated is more than nine, the Elections Chief Elections Officer/ElectionsOfficer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall intimate to the Society in writing the names of each of the

candidates, the symbols, if any, allotted to each such candidate, the date when the election will be conducted, the time andplace of such election to enable the Society to have the posters, copied, cyclostyled or printed and exhibited and the ballotpapers to be printed and handed over to such Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant ElectionsOfficer.
8.3 The Poll shall commence at 9 a,m. and close at 4. p.m. on the day notified by the Chief Elections Officer/ElectionsOfficer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer.
8.4 Voting shall be on ballot papers issued by the Assistant Elections Officer under Rule 11.2 of these Rules bearinghis imprint of his seal in addition.
ALLOCATION OF SYMBOLS TO CANDIDATES

9.1 The Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall use suchnumber of symbols as there are candidates and the symbols so selected shall be the symbols in serial order commencing from1 as printed on the ballot paper.

For example:- if there are fifteen candidates, the symbols 1 to 15 shall be used. Each candidate shall be assigned asymbol from among these symbols by the draw of lots. The Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall maintain a record of the symbols assigned to each candidate.
BALLOT PAPERS
10. 1. Each Ballot Paper shall be printed as specified in Schedule ‘D’ of these rules.
11.1 The Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall preside at theelections.

11.2 Prior to the issue of Ballot Papers, the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/AssistantElections Officer shall strike off such the symbols that have not been allocated to any of the candidates and shall affix theBranch Seal on each Ballot Paper used and sign thereon.

11.3 Any person whose name appears in the Voters’ List of the Branch shall be entitled so a Ballot Paper on proof ofhis identity by the production of his National Identity Card or valid Motor Driving License or valid Passport or valid Identitycard with the photograph issued by the employer or the Pension Identity Card or other similar document acceptable to ChiefElections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer.
11.4 Before a Ballot Paper is issued to a voter, the person issuing the Ballot Paper shall first satisfy himself that thevoter’s name appears in the Voters’ List.
11.5 As and when each voter is given a Ballot Paper his name in the Voters’ List shall be marked.
11.6 No voter shall be issued more than ballot paper

11.7 A voter shall be entitled to cast only one vote to each candidate of his choice and the maximum number ofcandidates for whom he may vote shall be nine. If a voter votes for more than nine candidates, his Ballot Paper shall beconsidered spoilt.

11.8 On receipt of a Ballot Paper each voter shall indicate his preference on the given ballot paper by placing a markin the cage against each of the symbols and/or numbers of his choice and shall deposit the ballot paper in a receptacle placedwithin the view of the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer.

11.9. A voter, who is not able to mark a Ballot Paper due to any physical disability, may request the Chief ElectionsOfficer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone! Assistant Elections Officer to mark the ballot paper on his behalf.

11.10. The Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall declare thepoll closed at 4.00 p.m.
COUNTING

12.1. Immediately after the closure of the poll the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer with such assistance as is available will proceed to count the votes that are in the receptacle. Forthis purpose all votes which are not rejected by him under Rule 12.2 and 12.3 below shall be counted with the aid of scoresheets.
12.2. He shall reject any ballot paper which is marked for more than nine candidates.

12.3 Where in a ballot paper a mark is placed and it is not clear for which of two candidates the voter has voted, theChief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall have the power to reject suchvote and to accept the balance votes.
12.4 Where in a ballot paper a voter has made more than one mark in favour of a candidate, all such markings shallconstitute only one vote.

12.5. Where the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer rejects aballot paper under Rule 12.2 and 12.5 such rejected ballot papers shall be bound together, counted and reconciled with hisballot paper account.
ELECTION RESULTS
13.1 On the completion of the count, each of the nine candidates who receive more votes than each of the remainingcandidate shall be declared elected as members of the branch committee.

In the event of an equality of votes among two or more candidates, the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer shall, where necessary, decide, by the drawing of Jots, the candidate or candidatesamong them to be elected to the committee. However, such drawing of lots shall not be necessary where, even with anequality of votes amongst some candidates, the required number of candidates can be declared elected as members to theCommittee.

13.2 The Elections Officer/Assistant Elections Officer shall communicate the results of the election in writing to theSociety specifying the names of candidates declared elected to the Committee. A copy of this communication shall be sent bythe Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer to the Assistant Commissioner ofCo-operative Development of the area.
13.3. The Secretary of the Society shall display conspicuously for a period not less than 10 days the names of theelected members at the place of business and at the office of the particular branch.

14.1 The decision of the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer onany question arising in respect of the conduct of the poll, counting of votes, or communicating the results of the poll shallbe final and conclusive.
Part IV
MISCELLANEOUS
15.1 After the declaration of the results of the election, the Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge ofzone/Assistant Elections Officer shall ensure that: -
i. the unused ballot papers, the marked Voters List, all nomination papers and one copy of the journal referred
to in Rule 7.6 and 7.7 are enclosed in an envelope, sealed and sent to the Head;

ii. the spoilt ballot papers and the original copy of the journal referred to in Rules 7.6 and 7.7 of these Rules are
enclosed in a separate envelope, marked spoilt ballot papers and journal and sealed and sent to the Assistantof Co-operative Development of the area.
16. All expenses in connection with the elections to a branch committee of a Society shall be borne by that society.
17. The Commissioner shall have the power to add to, amend, to vary or to rescind these rules including allSchedules.
18. If any dispute arises regarding the interpretation of these Rules, the decision of the Commissioner shall be finaland conclusive.
Part V
INTERPRETATIONS
In these Rules :
19.1. ‘By-laws’ mean the registered by-laws of the society for the time being in force and include registered amendmentsof the by-laws;

19.2 Except in Rules 7 (2) (a), 17 and 18 ‘Commissioner’ shall mean and shall include the Commissioner of Co-operative Development or Deputy Commissioner of Co-operative Development or Senior Assistant Commissioner of Co-operative Development or Assistant Commissioner of Co-operative Development or any other person duly authorized byany of those above named,
19.3 In Rules 7 (2) (a), 17 and 18 the ‘Commissioner’ shall mean the North Western Provincial Commissioner /Registrar of Co-operative Development;

19.4 ‘The Chief Elections Officer/Elections Officer In-Charge of zone/Assistant Elections Officer’ shall mean thepersons appointed by the Assistant Commissioner in charge of the division for the particular branch of society under theseRules.

19.5 ‘Voter’ shall mean the person admitted to membership in ‘the Society from the area of operations of the branchwhose name is included in the voters’ list duly certified for-the purpose of elections to the said branch committee of theSociety.
19.6 ‘Co-operative Act’ shall mean the Co-operative Society Act or the Co-operative Society Statute for the timebeing in force in the North Western Province.
20. In the event of any inconsistence between the Sinhala and Tamil texts of these Rules, the Sinhala text shallprevail.
